current_episode.title: Advice Line with Daymond John of FUBU

guest.bio_context: Daymond John is the legendary founder of the streetwear clothing brand FUBU (For Us, By Us). He previously appeared on How I Built This in 2018, where he told the story of working at Red Lobster in his 20s in the early 1990s while building his clothing brand. He has since become a longtime judge on Shark Tank, as well as a speaker and author.

pending_qa.q: How did FUBU gain early brand awareness and traction before becoming a mainstream brand?
pending_qa.r: Daymond John credits mom-and-pop stores as the ones who made FUBU, explaining that store owners told customers that the four young men behind the brand were working hard, producing quality goods that were moving faster than Nike, and offered a compelling local story. He contrasts this with big-box stores where employees are disengaged and not telling the brand story. He advises early-stage founders to identify smaller independent stores, go in, talk to customers, and hand out samples to build brand awareness and understand how the product will work at scale.

pending_qa.q: What is the business model and social impact of Cooks Who Feed, the kitchen linen company based in Canada?
pending_qa.r: Cooks Who Feed is a for-profit social enterprise based in the Niagara region near Toronto, Canada, founded about six years ago. The company produces kitchen linens — including chef aprons, tea towels, grocery totes, wine totes, linen napkins, and custom hospitality items — and operates a meal give-back model that has provided around two million meals to those in need through product sales. The company owns its own production facility just north of Delhi, where it hires women from surrounding villages and trains them as seamstresses, providing safe and fair employment.

pending_qa.q: What is Raised Nutrition and what makes its protein bar different from competitors?
pending_qa.r: Raised Nutrition, founded by Darcy and his wife Jess and based in Ballina, New South Wales, Australia, makes whole food protein bars free from artificial flavors, sweeteners, preservatives, fillers, and natural flavors. The bars were originally designed for Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu athletes focused on injury recovery, featuring approximately five grams of Australian grass-fed collagen per bar combined with Australian pumpkin seed protein and organic sprouted brown rice protein. Despite targeting the Jiu-Jitsu community, the brand is finding broader appeal among runners, swimmers, and general health enthusiasts drawn to the clean-label, ingredient-transparent positioning.
